taxonomy:
## Taxonomy of grid-based logic games (from the provided rule texts)

### A) Illumination / visibility constraints
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated in row/column until black/edge; bulbs can’t see each other.
- **Kurodoko**: Color black cells so numbered cells count white cells to nearest black/edge; black cells can’t touch; all white cells connected.
- **Kurotto**: Color black cells so each numbered circle equals the sum of continuous black cells in four directions; circles can’t be colored.

### B) Loop / path drawing (single closed loop)
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Draw a single loop through cell centers; must pass all white-circle cells with area-wise straight/turn rule; must avoid black-circle cells.
- **Masyu**: Single loop through all circles; white circles require straight-through + at least one adjacent right turn; black circles require a turn then straight.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop with direction; must pass arrow cells; wind direction blocks movement against wind and constrains entry.
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop through all black circles; each black circle is midpoint of the straight segment passing through it.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop; each bold-bordered room visited exactly once; in each room loop passes either all moon cells or all sun cells; alternates room types.
- **Slitherlink**: Single loop through dots; numbered cells constrain how many surrounding edges are used.
- **Suraromu**: Single loop through cell centers; must pass all “gates” (dotted segments) exactly once; starts/returns to open numbered circle; gate numbers constrain crossing order.
- **Yajilin**: Single loop through cell centers; numbers on arrows constrain direction counts; loop must avoid black-number cells; black cells can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Yosenabe**: Not a loop; included here only if you interpret “tracks” as movement, but rules describe moving circles into gray areas (see section E).

### C) Region partitioning / tiling / rectangle-based decomposition
- **Chained Block**: Partition into blocks of consecutive black cells; each block has a size number or “?”; blocks form chains with corner contact; no duplicate shapes in a chain.
- **Double Choco**: Divide grid into blocks by solid lines; each block contains two same-form areas (white/gray) possibly rotated/reflected; block number equals half the block’s colored count.
- **Evolomino**: Fill board with numbers by blocks; each block has size equal to its number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Five Cells**: Partition into blocks of exactly 5 cells; numbered cells count surrounding lines including outer frame; lines can’t enter blocks.
- **Fillomino**: Fill empty cells with numbers; blocks are formed by equal numbers; block size equals the number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect islands with bridges; bridge counts per island; bridges can’t cross islands/bridges; all islands linked.
- **Heyawake**: Bold-bordered rooms; numbers count painted cells; white cells can’t span more than two rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells can’t be separated by painted cells.
- **Nurimeizu**: Outlined regions each contain exactly two blocks of equal size/number; blocks are connected shaded cells; shaded cells connected across region boundaries; two blocks in same region can’t touch orthogonally; no fully shaded 2×2.
- **Nurimisaki**: Circle cells remain white and are “Misaki”; non-circle white cells can’t be Misaki; Misaki has exactly one adjacent white cell; circle numbers count straight-line white length; all white connected; no 2×2 of either color.
- **Makaro**: Rooms enclosed by bold lines; each room contains all numbers up to its cell count; arrow cells: biggest number among up/down/left/right neighbors determines the target cell; same number can’t be adjacent across rooms.
- **Shikaku**: Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its area (cell count).
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles in squares; uncovered white cells must form a rectangle or square; numbers count black triangles around (orthogonally).
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-bordered “Tiles”; color tiles so diagonal-line clues specify required black counts to the right/down along the diagonal’s row/column until boundary/another diagonal; all cells in a tile are either all colored or all uncolored.
- **Sto-stone**: Bold-bordered Rooms; room number gives count of continuous black cells; black cells can’t connect across bold lines; when stones “drop” straight down, bottom half must be filled with no empty cells (dropped stones may cross/connect across bold lines).
- **Sashigane**: Divide into L-shaped blocks (one cell wide); open circles mark the knee; arrow cells mark an end pointing toward the knee; each block has 0–3 marks (arrows/open circles).
- **Satogaeri**: Bold-bordered “Countries”; move circles orthogonally so each country has exactly one circle; circle numbers indicate how many cells it must pass through; some circles don’t move; circles can’t cross tracks or other circles.
- **Juosan**: Bold-bordered territories; fill each cell with “—” or “|”; territory numbers constrain how many additional marks it gets; “—” and “|” have max run lengths in orthogonal directions.

### D) Coloring / shading / black-white placement with connectivity or adjacency rules
- **Choco Banana**: Paint some cells black; orthogonally connected black cells must form rectangles/squares; orthogonally connected white cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate size of the area containing the cell.
- **Hitori**: Color cells so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells never touch orthogonally; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Kurodoko**: (also fits A) black/white connectivity and non-touching constraints.
- **LITS**: Color tetrominoes (4 consecutive squares) in each bold area; similarly shaped rotated/reflected tetrominoes can’t touch except at corners; colored squares form a connected network; no 2×2 or larger colored squares.
- **Nurikabe**: Fill with black wall cells and white regions; numbers give size of continuous white cells; each white area has one number; black cells form a continuous wall; black cells can’t form 2×2.
- **Nuritwin**: Shade cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of same number of cells; blocks are connected shaded cells; all shaded cells connected across region boundaries; two blocks in same region can’t touch orthogonally; no fully shaded 2×2.
- **Heyawake**: (also fits C) painted/white connectivity and separation constraints.
- **Usowan**: Color some cells; cells with numbers can’t be colored; each rectangle bordered by bold lines has exactly one wrong number (wrong colored-cell count); colored cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells can’t be separated by colored cells.
- **Yajilin**: (also fits B) includes black-cell non-touching and loop avoidance.
- **Shakashaka**: (also fits C) black triangles placement with rectangle/square uncovered white constraint.

### E) Movement / routing of entities (non-loop)
- **Hebi**: Place sequential snake numbers 1→5 in white squares; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; directional “view” constraints with black squares and grid rim; black squares show nearest-square count in arrow direction.
- **Nansuke**: Fill blank cells with digits from a list; each cell has one digit; numbers are either vertical (up-down) or horizontal (left-right).
- **Norinori**: Place blocks in pairs in consecutive black squares.
- **Pencils**: Draw pencil lines from tips through cell centers; each pencil is a straight group with tip at one end; numbers in pencil cells give length; pencil line can’t cross or branch; line passes through as many cells as the number.
- **Ripple Effect**: Rooms (bold lines) each contain consecutive numbers starting from 1; if a number duplicates in a row/column, the distance between duplicates must be ≥ that number.
- **Satogaeri**: (also fits C) moving circles through countries with track constraints.
- **Yosenabe**: Move all circles orthogonally into gray areas; arrow shows movement direction with tip in a gray cell; arrows don’t bend and don’t cross other circles/lines; number in gray area equals sum of entering circle numbers; empty gray areas unrestricted but at least one circle must enter some gray area.
- **Numberlink**: Connect pairs of equal numbers with continuous lines; lines go through cell centers orthogonally/turning; lines can’t cross/branch; lines can’t go through number cells.
- **Hashiwokakero**: (also fits C) bridges are a routing/connectivity constraint.

### F) Pure arithmetic / constraint satisfaction (grid numbers with local/global rules)
- **Sudoku**: Place 1–9 in each empty cell; each row/column/3×3 block contains all 1–9.
- **Nansuke**: Digits from a list with orientation constraint (up-down or left-right).
- **Makaro**: Room-based “up to N” number sets and arrow-based max-to-target rule.
- **Ripple Effect**: Consecutive numbering per room and duplication-distance constraint.
- **Chained Block**: Block size numbers and “?” uncertainty (arithmetic on block sizes).
- **Choco Banana**: Numbers indicate area size of connected region containing the cell.

### G) Snake/sequence-like or ordered placement (explicit ordering)
- **Hebi**: Ordered snake head-to-tail 1→5 with directional attack constraints.
- **Ripple Effect**: Consecutive numbers starting from 1 within each room.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Ordered alternation of room types as the loop progresses (moon rooms then sun rooms, etc.).

If you want, I can also output this taxonomy as a JSON structure (game → categories) or as a hierarchical tree.
